def _make_audit_hook(
    *, mode: str, read_roots: tuple[str, ...], read_exact: frozenset[str], code_roots: tuple[str, ...],
    write_roots: tuple[str, ...], endpoint: str | None, endpoint_is_dir: bool, forbid_paths: tuple[str, ...],
    forbidden: tuple[str, ...], snapshot: frozenset[str], modules: dict[str, Any], counter: Any, err_fd: int,
    protected: frozenset[int], nowrite_roots: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> tuple[Callable[[str, tuple[Any, ...]], None], Callable[[], None]]:
    """The audit hook and the atexit check, closures over immutable values and C builtins only.

    ``nowrite_roots`` (lower-cased realpaths) are carved out of ``write_roots``: no write or filesystem
    change under them, whatever the case of the path (a case-insensitive volume maps ``FWD`` to ``fwd``).

    Markers go to ``err_fd`` (a private duplicate of stderr); ``counter`` is shared with the actions
    hook and the monitor. The hook holds no exit or close function: a frame of it seen on a traceback
    gives nothing that ends the process without the status-3 check."""
    is_client = mode == KERNEL_CLIENT
    t = _type_table()
    type_, str_t, int_t, tuple_t, list_t = type, str, int, tuple, list
    repr_, len_ = repr, len
    realpath, under, coerce = _hn_realpath, _hn_under, _hn_path
    lstat, readlink, getcwd, write, audit = posix.lstat, posix.readlink, posix.getcwd, posix.write, sys.audit
    note = counter.__next__
    IOV, IMV, GV = IOViolation, ImportViolation, GuardViolation
    list_events, fs_change, os_allowed, refused = _LIST_EVENTS, _FS_CHANGE, _OS_ALLOWED, _ALWAYS_REFUSED
    code_sfx = CODE_SUFFIXES
    af_unix = socket.AF_UNIX
    w_flags = posix.O_WRONLY | posix.O_RDWR | posix.O_APPEND | posix.O_CREAT | posix.O_TRUNC
    label = "KERNEL_CLIENT" if is_client else "BUILD_EDIT"
    stdout, stderr = sys.__stdout__, sys.__stderr__
    lower = str.lower
    nowrite = tuple(lower(r) for r in nowrite_roots)

    def hook(event: str, args: tuple[Any, ...]) -> None:
        if event == "hn_guard.violation":
            note()
            try:
                write(err_fd, ("HN_GUARD: refused: " + str_t(args[0])[:400] + "\n").encode("utf-8", "replace"))
            except:  # noqa: E722  (a closed or full stderr loses the line, never the status 3)
                pass
            return None
        msg = None
        exc = IOV
        if event == "open" or event in list_events:
            target = args[0] if args else None
            if target is None and event != "open":
                target = "."
            p = coerce(target, t)
            if type_(p) is int_t:
                if p in protected:
                    msg = "a file object on the guard's stderr (fd 2 or its private copy)"
                else:
                    return None  # an already open descriptor
            if msg is not None:
                pass
            elif p is None:
                msg = "file access through an unsupported path object " + repr_(type_(target))
            else:
                rp = realpath(p, getcwd(), lstat, readlink)
                mode_arg = args[1] if len_(args) > 1 else None
                flags = args[2] if len_(args) > 2 else 0
                is_write = False
                if event == "open":
                    if type_(mode_arg) is str_t:
                        is_write = ("w" in mode_arg) or ("a" in mode_arg) or ("x" in mode_arg) or ("+" in mode_arg)
                    if type_(flags) is int_t and flags & w_flags:
                        is_write = True
                kernel = endpoint is not None and rp is not None and (
                    rp == endpoint or (endpoint_is_dir and rp.startswith(endpoint + "/") and rp.count("/") == endpoint.count("/") + 1)
                )
                if rp is None:
                    msg = "file access to an undecidable path (symlink loop)"
                elif under(rp, forbid_paths):
                    msg = "reading the source of a forbidden module " + rp[:200]
                elif event == "open" and mode_arg is None and not kernel:
                    try:
                        is_dir = (lstat(rp).st_mode & 0o170000) == 0o040000
                    except:  # noqa: E722
                        is_dir = False
                    if is_dir:
                        msg = "opening a directory descriptor " + rp[:200]
                if msg is None:
                    if is_write:
                        if not (is_client and (kernel or under(rp, write_roots))):
                            msg = "write to " + rp[:200] + (" (writes go under output/<phase>/)" if is_client else " (no writes in build_edit.py)")
                        elif not kernel and under(lower(rp), nowrite):
                            msg = "write to " + rp[:200] + " (output/<phase>/fwd/ is written only by ./fwd)"
                    elif is_client:
                        if not (kernel or under(rp, read_roots)):
                            msg = "read of " + rp[:200] + " (outside the author directory and the interpreter install)"
                    elif not (rp in read_exact or (under(rp, code_roots) and (event != "open" or rp.endswith(code_sfx)))):
                        msg = "read of " + rp[:200] + " (build_edit.py reads only its constants file)"
        elif event in refused:
            msg = event + (" (no subprocesses, threads, tracing, gc introspection, mmap or links)")
        elif event in fs_change:
            if not is_client:
                msg = event + " (no filesystem changes in build_edit.py)"
            else:
                pos, fds = fs_change[event]
                for i in fds:  # CPython reports an unset dir_fd as -1
                    if len_(args) > i and args[i] is not None and args[i] != -1:
                        msg = event + " with dir_fd"
                for i in pos:
                    if msg is None and len_(args) > i:
                        p = coerce(args[i], t)
                        rp = realpath(p, getcwd(), lstat, readlink) if type_(p) is str_t else None
                        if rp is None or not under(rp, write_roots):
                            msg = event + " on " + (rp or repr_(type_(args[i])))[:200] + " (outside output/<phase>/)"
                        elif under(lower(rp), nowrite):
                            msg = event + " on " + rp[:200] + " (output/<phase>/fwd/ is written only by ./fwd)"
        elif event.startswith("socket."):
            if is_client and event == "socket.__new__" and len_(args) > 1 and args[1] == af_unix:
                return None
            if is_client and event == "socket.connect" and endpoint is not None and len_(args) > 1:
                p = coerce(args[1], t)
                rp = realpath(p, getcwd(), lstat, readlink) if type_(p) is str_t else None
                if rp is not None and (rp == endpoint or (endpoint_is_dir and rp.startswith(endpoint + "/"))):
                    return None
            msg = event + " (the only connection allowed is the kernel endpoint)"
        elif event.startswith("ctypes."):
            msg = event + " (no ctypes)"
        elif event.startswith("os."):
            if event in os_allowed:
                return None
            msg = event + " (not on the guard's list of allowed os operations)"
        elif event == "import":
            name = args[0] if args else ""
            if type_(name) is str_t:
                for pre in forbidden:
                    if name == pre or name.startswith(pre + "."):
                        msg = "import of forbidden module " + name
                if msg is None and name in snapshot and name not in modules:
                    msg = "re-import of " + name + " after it was removed from sys.modules"
            exc = IMV
        elif event == "object.__setattr__":
            if len_(args) > 1 and args[1] == "__code__":
                msg = "assignment to a function's __code__"
            exc = GV
        elif event == "hn_guard.count":
            if args and type_(args[0]) is list_t:
                r = repr_(counter)  # "count(N)": reading it does not advance it
                args[0].append(int_t(r[6:-1]))
            return None
        elif event == "hn_guard.mode":
            if args and type_(args[0]) is list_t:
                args[0].append(label)
            return None
        if msg is None:
            return None
        note()
        try:
            write(err_fd, ("HN_GUARD: refused: " + msg + "\n").encode("utf-8", "replace"))
        except:  # noqa: E722
            pass
        raise exc(msg + " refused by the hn_guard " + label + " guard")

    def at_exit() -> None:
        for s in (stdout, stderr):
            try:
                s.flush()
            except:  # noqa: E722
                pass
        audit("hn_guard.exit_check")  # the actions hook exits with status 3 if any violation was recorded

    return hook, at_exit


_ACTIONS = frozenset({"hn_guard.exit", "hn_guard.abort", "hn_guard.close", "hn_guard.exit_check", "hn_guard.fatal"})


def _make_actions_hook(
    *, counter: Any, err_fd: int, protected: frozenset[int], originals: tuple[Any, Any, Any],
) -> Callable[[str, tuple[Any, ...]], None]:
    """The second audit hook, the only holder of the original ``_exit`` / ``abort`` / ``close``.

    It never raises and calls only C functions on exact ints and bytes, so no frame of it is ever on a
    traceback or under attacker code. ``hn_guard.exit`` / ``abort`` / ``exit_check`` / ``fatal``: once
    any violation was recorded (or for ``fatal``) it writes a marker to ``err_fd`` and exits with
    status 3; otherwise it exits with the given status, aborts, or (``exit_check``) returns.
    ``hn_guard.close``: closes the descriptor unless it is protected, reporting into the given list.
    ``originals``: ``posix._exit``, ``posix.abort`` and ``posix.close`` taken before they were patched."""
    type_, int_t, list_t, len_, repr_ = type, int, list, len, repr
    write = posix.write
    exit_, abort_, close_ = originals
    acts, fatal, ebadf, status_v, oserror = _ACTIONS, _FATAL, errno.EBADF, EXIT_VIOLATION, OSError

    def actions(event: str, args: tuple[Any, ...]) -> None:
        if event not in acts:  # the event name is always an exact str (CPython builds it from C)
            return None
        if event == "hn_guard.close":
            if len_(args) == 2 and type_(args[1]) is list_t:
                fd = args[0]
                if type_(fd) is not int_t or fd < 0 or fd > 2147483647:
                    args[1].append(ebadf)
                elif fd in protected:
                    args[1].append(-1)
                else:
                    try:
                        close_(fd)
                    except oserror as e:
                        en = e.errno
                        args[1].append(en if type_(en) is int_t else ebadf)
            return None
        r = repr_(counter)  # "count(N)"
        if event == "hn_guard.fatal":
            msg = fatal
        elif r != "count(0)":
            msg = ("HN_GUARD: " + r[6:-1] + " violation(s) during this run; exit status 3\n").encode()
        elif event == "hn_guard.abort":
            abort_()
            return None
        elif event == "hn_guard.exit":
            code = args[0] if len_(args) == 1 else 1
            if type_(code) is not int_t or code < -2147483648 or code > 2147483647:
                code = 1
            exit_(code)
            return None
        else:
            return None  # exit_check with no violation: the interpreter finishes normally
        try:
            write(err_fd, msg)
        except:  # noqa: E722
            pass
        exit_(status_v)
        return None

    return actions

_MON_MUTATORS = ("use_tool_id", "free_tool_id", "register_callback", "set_events", "set_local_events", "restart_events")
_TOOL_PREFERENCE = (3, 4, 5, 2, 1, 0)
_FATAL = b"HN_GUARD: grad mode was found enabled (a path the patches do not cover); exiting with status 3\n"
# Builtin (C) callables refused by name wherever they are reached (v0.3 IO list + process/subclass escapes).
BANNED_BUILTIN_NAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({

def _make_monitor(
    *, banned: frozenset[int], sge_id: int, inference_id: int, op_banned: frozenset[str], op_types: tuple[type, ...],
    instance_types: frozenset[int], script_types: frozenset[int], script_names: frozenset[str],
    rng_ids: frozenset[int], rng_py_ids: frozenset[int], rng_c_types: frozenset[int], rng_ok: frozenset[str],
    np_rng_types: frozenset[int], tok_types: frozenset[int], mon_ns: Any, imp_mod: Any, snapshot: frozenset[str],
    modules: dict[str, Any], forbidden: tuple[str, ...], ext_roots: tuple[str, ...], forbid_paths: tuple[str, ...],
    spec_type: type, counter: Any, protected: frozenset[int],
) -> tuple[Callable[..., Any], Callable[..., Any], Callable[..., Any]]:
    """CALL / C_RETURN / PY_START callbacks, closures over immutable values and C builtins only.

    They hold no exit function: grad mode found on, or a direct ``_exit`` / ``abort`` after a
    violation, is ended by the actions hook (``hn_guard.fatal`` / ``hn_guard.exit``)."""
    is_grad = torch._C.is_grad_enabled
    audit = sys.audit
    id_, type_, str_t, vars_, getattr_, int_t, repr_ = id, type, str, vars, getattr, int, repr
    builtin_t, method_t, missing = types.BuiltinFunctionType, types.MethodType, sys.monitoring.MISSING
    module_t = types.ModuleType
    GV, IOV = GuardViolation, IOViolation
    exit_names, fd_names, status_v = EXIT_NAMES, FD_NAMES, EXIT_VIOLATION
    mutators = frozenset(_MON_MUTATORS)
    banned_names, tok_names = BANNED_BUILTIN_NAMES, TOKENIZERS_IO_NAMES
    realpath, under, refuse, mro_ids = _hn_realpath, _hn_under, _hn_refuse, _hn_mro_ids
    lstat, readlink, getcwd = posix.lstat, posix.readlink, posix.getcwd
    rng_callers = rng_ok | {random.__file__}
    no_rng = " (random numbers come only from hn_guard.control_normal)"

    def on_call(code: Any, offset: int, c: Any, arg0: Any) -> None:
        if is_grad():
            audit("hn_guard.fatal")  # exits with status 3
        i = id_(c)
        if i in banned:
            if i == sge_id:
                if arg0 is missing or arg0:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "grad mode enabled through an original torch._C._set_grad_enabled reference")
                return None
            if i == inference_id:
                if arg0 is not missing and not arg0:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "inference_mode(False) through an original torch._C._InferenceMode reference")
                return None
            nm = getattr_(c, "__qualname__", None) or getattr_(c, "__name__", "?")
            refuse(audit, GV, "call of a banned original (" + str_t(nm)[:120] + ")")
        tc = type_(c)
        if tc is method_t:  # a bound Python function, or a pybind11 instancemethod bound to an object
            f = c.__func__
            if id_(f) in banned:
                refuse(audit, GV, "call of a banned original method")
            if id_(f) in rng_ids:
                refuse(audit, GV, "numpy random generator method" + no_rng)
            if id_(f) in rng_py_ids and code.co_filename not in rng_callers:
                refuse(audit, GV, "random.Random method" + no_rng)
            name = str_t(getattr_(f, "__name__", ""))
            s = c.__self__
            for k in mro_ids(type_(s), id_):
                if k in instance_types:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "method " + name + " of a banned engine, file reader or compiler object")
                if k in script_types and name in script_names:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "TorchScript " + name)
                if k in np_rng_types:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "numpy random generator method " + name + no_rng)
                if k in tok_types and name in tok_names:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "tokenizers file I/O " + name)
            return None
        if tc is builtin_t:
            name = c.__name__
            s = c.__self__
            if name in banned_names:
                refuse(audit, GV, "call of " + name + " (a file reader, process launcher or subclass enumeration)")
            if s is mon_ns and name in mutators:
                refuse(audit, GV, "sys.monitoring." + name)
            st = type_(s)
            if st is module_t and name in exit_names and repr_(counter) != "count(0)":
                audit("hn_guard.exit", status_v)  # any posix._exit / abort, even of a re-created posix
            if (st is module_t or st is type_) and name in fd_names and type_(arg0) is int_t and arg0 in protected:
                refuse(audit, IOV, name + " on the guard's stderr (fd 2 or its private copy)")
            ids = mro_ids(s, id_) if st is type_ else mro_ids(st, id_)
            for k in ids:
                if k in instance_types:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "method " + name + " of a banned engine, file reader or compiler object")
                if k in script_types and name in script_names:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "TorchScript " + name)
                if k in np_rng_types:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "numpy random generator method " + name + no_rng)
                if k in tok_types and name in tok_names:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "tokenizers file I/O " + name)
                if k in rng_c_types and code.co_filename not in rng_callers:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "random.Random method " + name + no_rng)
            if name in op_banned and st.__name__.startswith("pybind11"):
                refuse(audit, GV, "JIT operator " + name)
            if s is imp_mod and (name == "create_dynamic" or name == "create_builtin"):
                if type_(arg0) is not spec_type or "name" in vars_(spec_type) or "origin" in vars_(spec_type):
                    refuse(audit, GV, "_imp." + name + " with a non-standard spec")
                d = vars_(arg0)
                mod = d.get("name")
                if type_(mod) is not str_t:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "_imp." + name + " without a module name")
                for pre in forbidden:
                    if mod == pre or mod.startswith(pre + "."):
                        refuse(audit, GV, "loading the forbidden module " + mod)
                if mod in snapshot and mod not in modules:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "re-creating " + mod + " after it was removed from sys.modules")
                if mod in modules:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "a second instance of the loaded module " + mod)
                if name == "create_dynamic":
                    origin = d.get("origin")
                    rp = realpath(origin, getcwd(), lstat, readlink) if type_(origin) is str_t else None
                    if rp is None or not under(rp, ext_roots) or under(rp, forbid_paths):
                        refuse(audit, GV, "loading an extension module from outside the interpreter install")
            return None
        if i in rng_ids:
            refuse(audit, GV, "numpy random generator method" + no_rng)
        if i in rng_py_ids and code.co_filename not in rng_callers:
            refuse(audit, GV, "random.Random method" + no_rng)
        if tc is type_:
            for k in mro_ids(c, id_):
                if k in rng_c_types and code.co_filename not in rng_ok:
                    refuse(audit, GV, "random.Random construction" + no_rng)
            return None
        if tc in op_types:
            q = getattr_(c, "_qualified_op_name", None)
            if q is None:
                q = getattr_(getattr_(c, "_overloadpacket", None), "_qualified_op_name", None) or getattr_(c, "_name", "")
            base = str_t(q).split("::")[-1].split(".")[0]
            if base in op_banned:
                refuse(audit, GV, "torch.ops operator " + base)
        return None

    def on_c_return(code: Any, offset: int, c: Any, arg0: Any) -> None:
        if is_grad():
            audit("hn_guard.fatal")  # exits with status 3
        return None

    def on_py_start(code: Any, offset: int) -> None:
        refuse(audit, GV, "execution of the original " + str_t(code.co_qualname)[:120])

    return on_call, on_c_return, on_py_start

"""``./py SCRIPT [ARGS...]``: one author script under the KERNEL_CLIENT guard (docs/V04_WSP_KERNEL.md §4-5).

    ./py output/<phase>/scratch/check.py [ARGS...]
    ./py -m py_compile output/<phase>/build_edit.py      (a syntax check; nothing is executed or written)

Installed as ``tools/hn_kernel/run_py.py`` (read-only, checked by ``hypaqwen.wsp.install.verify_tools``) and run
by the ``./py`` wrapper as ``.venv/bin/python -I -B tools/hn_kernel/run_py.py``. The v0.3 launcher
(``experiments/v0_3/author_kit/launch.py``) put the author's directories on ``sys.path``; this one never
does, because everything it runs before the guard is unguarded:

1. ``sys.path`` is scrubbed before the first non-builtin import, as in ``fwd.py``: ``''``, this directory
   and every entry inside the author dir are dropped, except the interpreter install (the author venv,
   ``AUTHOR_DIR/.venv``, read-only). A ``json.py`` or ``numpy/`` planted in ``output/`` or ``tools/``
   is therefore never imported.
2. The tools directories must be read-only (``tools/``, ``tools/hn_kernel/``, ``tools/hn_guard/``), so
   nothing can be planted next to the files loaded by path below.
3. The standard library, ``numpy``, ``torch``, ``safetensors`` and ``tokenizers`` are imported; the
   kernel client is loaded by explicit path (``client.py`` as ``hn_kernel_client``, which loads
   ``protocol.py``) and builds ``tok`` from ``packet/qwen/tokenizer.json``; ``wsp.py`` is loaded by path
   as the module ``wsp``, so ``from wsp import ...`` resolves to this installed client and nothing else;
   the guard package is loaded by path as ``hn_guard``.
4. The phase is ``$HN_PHASE`` (set by the launcher), else the single ``output/<phase>/`` directory (the
   single writable one if there are several). The script must be a ``.py`` file inside
   ``output/<phase>/``; ``-c`` and every ``-m`` other than ``py_compile`` are refused.
5. ``hn_guard.install(KERNEL_CLIENT, author_dir=AUTHOR_DIR, phase=..., kernel_endpoint=AUTHOR_DIR/.kernel/kernel.sock)``.
   From here on the guard holds for the life of the process: reads only under the author dir and the
   interpreter install, writes only under ``output/<phase>/``, one socket (the kernel), no subprocess,
   thread, autograd, optimiser or RNG (except ``wsp.control_direction``).
6. Only then is author code reachable. A finder appended at the end of ``sys.meta_path`` (after every
   standard finder, so it can never shadow the standard library or an installed package) resolves a
   top-level ``import name`` to ``name.py`` in the script's directory, then each parent up to
   ``output/<phase>/``, then ``packet/``. The script runs with ``runpy.run_path`` as ``__main__``.
7. The process ends with ``hn_guard.finish(code)``: the script's exit status, 1 after an uncaught
   exception, and 3 whenever the guard recorded a violation (even one the script caught).

Exit status 2: the command line, the phase or the tools layout was refused before any author code ran.
"""

# No ``from __future__`` import: it would be the first module looked up on sys.path (see fwd.py).
import os  # frozen, already loaded at start-up
import sys  # builtin

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(_HERE))  # AUTHOR_DIR (this file is AUTHOR_DIR/tools/hn_kernel/run_py.py)


def _inside(path: str, root: str) -> bool:
    return path == root or path.startswith(root.rstrip(os.sep) + os.sep)


def _install_roots() -> list:
    return [os.path.realpath(p) for p in (sys.prefix, sys.base_prefix, sys.exec_prefix, sys.base_exec_prefix)
            if p and os.path.realpath(p) != os.sep]


def _scrub_sys_path() -> None:
    """Drop '' (the cwd), this directory and the author dir from sys.path, keeping the interpreter install."""
    installs = _install_roots()
    keep = []
    for p in sys.path:
        r = os.path.realpath(p) if p else ""
        if not p or _inside(r, _HERE):
            continue
        if _inside(r, ROOT) and not any(_inside(r, i) for i in installs):
            continue
        keep.append(p)
    sys.path[:] = keep


if not __package__:  # run as the ./py launcher (as a package module, the harness's own sys.path is left alone)
    _scrub_sys_path()

import importlib.abc  # noqa: E402
import importlib.util  # noqa: E402
import re  # noqa: E402
import runpy  # noqa: E402
import stat  # noqa: E402
import traceback  # noqa: E402
import contextlib  # noqa: E402,F401  (protocol's and client's imports, loaded before them)
import json  # noqa: E402,F401
import math  # noqa: E402,F401
import socket  # noqa: E402,F401
import struct  # noqa: E402,F401
import typing  # noqa: E402,F401
import atexit  # noqa: E402,F401
from pathlib import Path  # noqa: E402,F401

import numpy  # noqa: E402,F401
import torch  # noqa: E402,F401

try:  # optional in the venv; loaded before the guard so later use needs no file reads
    import safetensors  # noqa: E402,F401
    import safetensors.torch  # noqa: E402,F401
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    pass
try:
    import tokenizers  # noqa: E402,F401
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    pass

PHASE_ENV = "HN_PHASE"
AUTHOR_ENV = "HN_AUTHOR_DIR"
SOCKET_ENV = "HN_KERNEL_SOCKET"
PHASE_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*")
MODULE_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
USAGE = "usage: ./py output/<phase>/SCRIPT.py [ARGS...]  |  ./py -m py_compile output/<phase>/FILE.py"


class Refused(Exception):
    """The command line, phase or tools layout is not allowed; nothing of the author's ran."""


def _check_tools() -> None:
    """tools/, tools/hn_kernel/ and tools/hn_guard/ are real, read-only directories (nothing can be planted)."""
    tools = os.path.dirname(_HERE)
    for d in (tools, _HERE, os.path.join(tools, "hn_guard")):
        try:
            st = os.lstat(d)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            raise Refused(f"{os.path.relpath(d, ROOT)}/ is missing") from None
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
            raise Refused(f"{os.path.relpath(d, ROOT)} is not a directory")
        if st.st_mode & 0o222:
            raise Refused(f"{os.path.relpath(d, ROOT)}/ is writable; the kernel tools may not run")


def _load_path(key: str, path: str, package_dir: str = None):
    """``path`` loaded by explicit file location as ``sys.modules[key]`` (a package when ``package_dir``)."""
    mod = sys.modules.get(key)
    if mod is not None:
        return mod
    kw = {"submodule_search_locations": [package_dir]} if package_dir else {}
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(key, path, **kw)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[key] = mod
    try:
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    except BaseException:
        del sys.modules[key]
        raise
    return mod


def resolve_phase(root: str, env: str = None) -> str:
    """``$HN_PHASE`` if set, else the single (writable) directory under ``output/``."""
    out = os.path.join(root, "output")
    if env:
        if not PHASE_RE.fullmatch(env):
            raise Refused(f"bad phase name {env!r}")
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(out, env)):
            raise Refused(f"output/{env}/ does not exist")
        return env
    try:
        names = sorted(n for n in os.listdir(out) if PHASE_RE.fullmatch(n) and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(out, n)))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise Refused("output/ does not exist") from None
    if len(names) > 1:
        names = [n for n in names if os.access(os.path.join(out, n), os.W_OK)]
    if len(names) != 1:
        raise Refused(f"cannot tell the phase: output/ holds {len(names)} candidate directories and {PHASE_ENV} is unset")
    return names[0]


def resolve_script(arg: str, root: str, phase: str) -> str:
    """The real path of a ``.py`` file inside ``output/<phase>/``, or ``Refused``."""
    phase_dir = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, "output", phase))
    path = os.path.realpath(arg if os.path.isabs(arg) else os.path.join(os.getcwd(), arg))
    if not _inside(path, phase_dir) or path == phase_dir:
        raise Refused(f"scripts must lie inside output/{phase}/: {arg}")
    if not path.endswith(".py"):
        raise Refused(f"not a .py file: {arg}")
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise Refused(f"no such script: {arg}") from None
    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
        raise Refused(f"not a regular file: {arg}")
    return path


def parse_argv(argv: list, root: str, phase: str) -> tuple:
    """``("run", script, args)`` or ``("compile", file, [])``; ``Refused`` for anything else."""
    if not argv or argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):
        raise Refused(USAGE)
    if argv[0] == "-c":
        raise Refused("./py -c is not supported: write the code to a file under output/<phase>/ and run that")
    if argv[0] == "-m":
        if len(argv) != 3 or argv[1] != "py_compile":
            raise Refused("the only -m form is: ./py -m py_compile output/<phase>/FILE.py")
        return "compile", resolve_script(argv[2], root, phase), []
    if argv[0].startswith("-"):
        raise Refused(f"unknown option {argv[0]!r}; {USAGE}")
    return "run", resolve_script(argv[0], root, phase), list(argv[1:])


class AuthorModules(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder):
    """Top-level ``import name`` -> ``name.py`` in ``dirs`` (searched in order). Installed after the guard and
    after every other finder, so it only ever sees names nothing else could import."""

    def __init__(self, dirs):
        self.dirs = tuple(dirs)

    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
        if path is not None or not MODULE_RE.fullmatch(name):
            return None
        for d in self.dirs:
            f = os.path.join(d, name + ".py")
            if os.path.isfile(f):
                return importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, f)
        return None


def module_dirs(script: str, root: str, phase: str) -> list:
    """The script's directory, each parent up to ``output/<phase>/``, then ``packet/``."""
    phase_dir = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, "output", phase))
    dirs, d = [], os.path.dirname(script)
    while _inside(d, phase_dir):
        dirs.append(d)
        if d == phase_dir:
            break
        d = os.path.dirname(d)
    packet = os.path.join(root, "packet")
    return dirs + ([packet] if os.path.isdir(packet) else [])


def _prepare(argv: list) -> tuple:
    """Everything before the guard. Returns ``(guard module, phase, action, path, args)``."""
    env_root = os.environ.get(AUTHOR_ENV)
    if env_root and os.path.realpath(env_root) != os.path.realpath(ROOT):
        raise Refused(f"{AUTHOR_ENV} does not name the directory these tools are installed in")
    _check_tools()
    phase = resolve_phase(ROOT, os.environ.get(PHASE_ENV))
    action, path, args = parse_argv(argv, ROOT, phase)
    endpoint = os.path.join(ROOT, ".kernel", "kernel.sock")
    os.environ[AUTHOR_ENV] = ROOT  # the client reads both at import / connect time
    os.environ[SOCKET_ENV] = endpoint  # the one socket the guard permits
    os.environ[PHASE_ENV] = phase
    client = _load_path("hn_kernel_client", os.path.join(_HERE, "client.py"))
    client._cache["tok"] = client.init_tok()  # reads packet/qwen/tokenizer.json, before the guard
    _load_path("wsp", os.path.join(_HERE, "wsp.py"))
    gdir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(_HERE), "hn_guard")
    guard = _load_path("hn_guard", os.path.join(gdir, "__init__.py"), package_dir=gdir)
    return guard, phase, action, path, args, endpoint


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    try:
        guard, phase, action, path, args, endpoint = _prepare(argv)
    except Refused as exc:
        print(f"./py: refused: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    guard.install(guard.KERNEL_CLIENT, author_dir=ROOT, phase=phase, kernel_endpoint=endpoint)
    code = 0
    try:
        if action == "compile":
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                compile(f.read(), path, "exec", dont_inherit=True)
            print(f"./py: {os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)} compiles")
        else:
            sys.meta_path.append(AuthorModules(module_dirs(path, ROOT, phase)))
            sys.argv = [path] + args  # runpy sets argv[0] to the script's path in any case
            try:
                runpy.run_path(path, run_name="__main__")
            except SystemExit as exc:
                code = exc.code if isinstance(exc.code, int) else (0 if exc.code is None else 1)
    except BaseException:  # noqa: BLE001 - the script's own traceback; the guard has printed any refusal
        traceback.print_exc()
        code = 1
    guard.finish(code)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

123	class KernelClient:
124	    """One connection to the kernel socket. The server serves one connection at a time."""

126	    def __init__(self, path: Path | str | None = None, timeout: float | None = None):
127	        self.path = Path(path or os.environ.get(SOCKET_ENV) or AUTHOR_DIR / ".kernel" / "kernel.sock")
128	        self._sock = _P.connect(self.path, timeout)
129	
130	    def close(self) -> None:
131	        self._sock.close()

133	    def call(self, op: str, tensors: dict[str, np.ndarray] | None = None, **args) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
134	        _P.send_msg(self._sock, {"op": op, "args": args}, tensors)
135	        header, out = _P.recv_msg(self._sock)
136	        if not header.get("ok"):
137	            err = header.get("error") or {}
138	            raise _ERRORS.get(err.get("type"), KernelError)(err.get("message", "unknown error"))
139	        return header.get("result"), out

141	    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
142	        return tuple(self.call("names")[0])
143	
144	    def shapes(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]:
145	        return {k: tuple(v) for k, v in self.call("shapes")[0].items()}
146	
147	    def arch(self) -> dict:

157	        return torch.from_numpy(self.call("load_label_rows", original=original)[1]["rows"])
158	
159	    def save_edit(self, name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> EditReceipt:
160	        return EditReceipt(**self.call("save_edit", {"tensor": _wire(tensor, name)}, name=name)[0])
161	
162	    def save_label_rows(self, rows: torch.Tensor) -> EditReceipt:
163	        return EditReceipt(**self.call("save_label_rows", {"rows": _wire(rows, "label rows")})[0])
164	
165	    def drop_edit(self, name: str) -> bool:
166	        return bool(self.call("drop_edit", name=name)[0]["dropped"])

171	    def edit_hash(self) -> str:

183	_client: KernelClient | None = None
184	_cache: dict[str, Any] = {}

187	def connect(path: Path | str | None = None) -> KernelClient:
188	    """(Re)open the module's connection, e.g. to a socket other than the default.
189	
190	    The server's metadata is fetched again; ``tok`` is kept: it comes from the packet, and the ``./py``
191	    launcher builds it before the guard, which refuses the tokenizer's file read afterwards.
192	    """
193	    global _client
194	    if _client is not None:
195	        _client.close()

197	    for k in [k for k in _cache if k != "tok"]:
198	        del _cache[k]

202	def _c() -> KernelClient:
203	    return _client if _client is not None else connect()

212	def init_tok(path: Path | str | None = None):
213	    """The packet's ``tokenizers.Tokenizer`` (``$HN_TOKENIZER``, else ``AUTHOR_DIR/packet/qwen/tokenizer.json``).
214	
215	    None if ``tokenizers`` is not installed or the file is missing. The ``./py`` wrapper calls this
216	    before entering the guard, which forbids reading other files afterwards.
217	    """
218	    p = Path(path or os.environ.get(TOKENIZER_ENV) or AUTHOR_DIR / "packet" / "qwen" / "tokenizer.json")
219	    try:

226	_LAZY = {
227	    "NAMES": lambda: _c().names(),
228	    "SHAPES": lambda: _c().shapes(),
229	    "ARCH": lambda: _c().arch(),
230	    "LABEL_IDS": lambda: tuple(__getattr__("ARCH")["label_ids"]),

236	def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:  # PEP 562: metadata is fetched on first access

240	        return _cache[name]

259	    """Replace a whole tensor. Refused outside the edit scope; equal to the original drops the edit."""
260	    return _c().save_edit(name, tensor)

280	    """``{tokens_used, tokens_left, requests}`` of the phase's forward-pass budget."""

283	
284	def load_quota() -> dict:
285	    """``{bytes_used, bytes_left, bytes_quota, tensors}`` of the phase's weight-load quota.
286	
287	    ``load``/``load_original`` of a layer tensor (anything but the embedding and the final norm)
288	    you have not loaded before in this phase draws on it; loading it again is free.
289	    """
290	    return _c().load_quota()

293	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- weight-only helpers
294	
295	
296	class HeadSlice(NamedTuple):
297	    """One head's block of a weight matrix: ``weight == load(name).narrow(dim, start, stop - start)``."""
298	
299	    name: str
300	    dim: int
301	    start: int
302	    stop: int
303	    weight: torch.Tensor
304	
305	
306	def _f32(x: Any) -> torch.Tensor:
307	    return torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(x) if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) else x).float()
308	
309	
310	def _2d(w: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
311	    return w.reshape(w.shape[0], -1)
312	
313	
314	def svd(name: str, k: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
315	    """Top-``k`` ``U [m, k]``, ``S [k]``, ``Vh [k, n]`` of the current tensor (as ``[shape[0], -1]``), in float64."""
316	    u, s, vh = torch.linalg.svd(_2d(load(name)).double(), full_matrices=False)
317	    return u[:, :k].float(), s[:k].float(), vh[:k].float()
318	
319	
320	def _head_table(layer: int, head: int) -> dict[str, tuple[str, int, int, int]]:
321	    a = __getattr__("ARCH")
322	    if a["layer_types"][layer] == "full_attention":
323	        nh, nkv, hd = a["num_attention_heads"], a["num_key_value_heads"], a["head_dim"]
324	        if not 0 <= head < nh:
325	            raise ValueError(f"layer {layer} has query heads 0..{nh - 1}")
326	        kv = head // (nh // nkv)  # GQA: query head -> its shared key/value head
327	        step = 2 * hd if a.get("attn_output_gate") else hd  # q_proj rows per head: [q (hd), gate (hd)]
328	        t = {"q": ("self_attn.q_proj.weight", 0, head * step, head * step + hd),
329	             "k": ("self_attn.k_proj.weight", 0, kv * hd, (kv + 1) * hd),
330	             "v": ("self_attn.v_proj.weight", 0, kv * hd, (kv + 1) * hd),
331	             "o": ("self_attn.o_proj.weight", 1, head * hd, (head + 1) * hd)}
332	        if a.get("attn_output_gate"):
333	            t["gate"] = ("self_attn.q_proj.weight", 0, head * step + hd, (head + 1) * step)
334	        return t
335	    nk, nv = a["linear_num_key_heads"], a["linear_num_value_heads"]
336	    dk, dv = a["linear_key_head_dim"], a["linear_value_head_dim"]
337	    if not 0 <= head < nv:
338	        raise ValueError(f"layer {layer} has value heads 0..{nv - 1}")
339	    kh, kd = head // (nv // nk), nk * dk  # value head -> its key head; in_proj_qkv rows are [q | k | v]
340	    qkv = "linear_attn.in_proj_qkv.weight"
341	    return {"q": (qkv, 0, kh * dk, (kh + 1) * dk),
342	            "k": (qkv, 0, kd + kh * dk, kd + (kh + 1) * dk),
343	            "v": (qkv, 0, 2 * kd + head * dv, 2 * kd + (head + 1) * dv),
344	            "z": ("linear_attn.in_proj_z.weight", 0, head * dv, (head + 1) * dv),
345	            "b": ("linear_attn.in_proj_b.weight", 0, head, head + 1),
346	            "a": ("linear_attn.in_proj_a.weight", 0, head, head + 1),
347	            "o": ("linear_attn.out_proj.weight", 1, head * dv, (head + 1) * dv)}
348	
349	
350	def head_slice(layer: int, head: int, kind: str, W: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> HeadSlice:
351	    """One head's rows (``q``/``k``/``v``/``gate``/``z``/``a``/``b``) or output columns (``o``).
352	
353	    Full-attention layers: ``head`` is a query head (``k``/``v`` give its shared KV head). Gated
354	    DeltaNet layers: ``head`` is a value head (``q``/``k`` give its key head). ``W`` defaults to
355	    ``load(name)``; pass a tensor you are editing to slice that instead.
356	    """
357	    table = _head_table(layer, head)
358	    if kind not in table:
359	        raise ValueError(f"kind must be one of {sorted(table)} for layer {layer}")
360	    rest, dim, start, stop = table[kind]
361	    name = f"{PREFIX}layers.{layer}.{rest}"
362	    W = load(name) if W is None else W
363	    return HeadSlice(name, dim, start, stop, W.narrow(dim, start, stop - start).clone())
364	
365	
366	def zero_head(layer: int, head: int) -> tuple[str, torch.Tensor]:
367	    """``(name, W')``: the layer's output projection with this head's input columns zeroed."""
368	    s = head_slice(layer, head, "o")
369	    W = load(s.name)
370	    W.narrow(1, s.start, s.stop - s.start).zero_()
371	    return s.name, W
372	
373	
374	def top_writers(name: str, direction: Any, k: int = 10) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
375	    """The ``k`` units whose weight vectors most align with ``direction``: ``(indices, signed scores)``, by |score|.
376	
377	    If ``direction`` lives in the output space (``shape[0]``: ``o_proj``, ``down_proj``, ``out_proj``)
378	    the units are columns (what each input unit writes); otherwise in the input space (``shape[1]``,
379	    e.g. embedding rows) they are rows.
380	    """
381	    W, d = _2d(load(name)), _f32(direction).reshape(-1)
382	    if W.shape[0] == d.numel():
383	        scores = W.T @ d
384	    elif W.shape[1] == d.numel():
385	        scores = W @ d
386	    else:
387	        raise ValueError(f"{name} {tuple(W.shape)} has no dimension of size {d.numel()}")
388	    idx = scores.abs().topk(min(k, scores.numel())).indices
389	    return idx, scores[idx]
390	
391	
392	def project_out(W: torch.Tensor, u: Any, cols: Sequence[int] | None = None, alpha: float = 1.0) -> torch.Tensor:
393	    """``W - alpha * u (mask * (u^T W))`` with ``u`` normalised to unit length (``u`` in the row space).
394	
395	    ``cols`` limits the projection to those columns; ``alpha=1`` removes the ``u`` component exactly.
396	    """
397	    W = _f32(W)
398	    u = _f32(u).reshape(-1)
399	    u = u / torch.linalg.vector_norm(u)
400	    coef = u @ _2d(W)
401	    if cols is not None:
402	        mask = torch.zeros_like(coef)
403	        mask[list(cols)] = 1.0
404	        coef = coef * mask
405	    return W - alpha * torch.outer(u, coef).reshape(W.shape)
406	
407	
408	def rank1(W: torch.Tensor, a: Any, b: Any) -> torch.Tensor:
409	    """``W + a b^T``."""
410	    W = _f32(W)
411	    return W + torch.outer(_f32(a).reshape(-1), _f32(b).reshape(-1)).reshape(W.shape)
412	
413	
414	def _final_norm() -> tuple[torch.Tensor, float]:
415	    if "_final_norm" not in _cache:
416	        _cache["_final_norm"] = (load(FINAL_NORM), float(__getattr__("ARCH")["rms_norm_eps"]))
417	    return _cache["_final_norm"]
418	
419	
420	def label_lens(h: Any, original: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
421	    """The four label logits a residual ``h [..., d]`` would give: final ``(1 + w)`` RMSNorm, then the label rows.
422	
423	    For ``./fwd`` hidden states (``hidden.L<n>.npy``); at the last layer this reproduces the readout.
424	    """
425	    w, eps = _final_norm()
426	    h = _f32(h)
427	    x = h * torch.rsqrt(h.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps) * (1.0 + w)
428	    return x @ label_rows(original).T
429	
430	
431	def dla(vec: Any, resid: Any = None, original: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
432	    """Direct label attribution of a residual contribution ``vec [..., d]``: ``(vec * (1 + w)) / rms(resid) @ rows^T``.
433	
434	    ``resid`` is the full final residual the contribution sits in (its RMS freezes the norm's scale);
435	    without it the RMS factor is 1.
436	    """
437	    w, eps = _final_norm()
438	    x = _f32(vec) * (1.0 + w)
439	    if resid is not None:
440	        r = _f32(resid)
441	        x = x * torch.rsqrt(r.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
442	    return x @ label_rows(original).T
443	
444	
445	def diff_means(a: Any, b: Any) -> torch.Tensor:
446	    """``mean(a, 0) - mean(b, 0)``."""
447	    return _f32(a).mean(0) - _f32(b).mean(0)
448	
449	
450	# Where the guard's control_normal lives: the install layout (tools/hn_kernel/ next to tools/hn_guard/),
451	# then the source layout (author/client.py next to author/hn_guard/).
452	_GUARD_KEYS = ("hn_guard.guards_v04", "hypaqwen.wsp.author.hn_guard.guards_v04", "hn_kernel_guards_v04")
453	
454	
455	def _control_normal():
456	    """The guard's ``control_normal`` (the only RNG either guard allows; ``torch.Generator`` is refused).
457	
458	    Reuses the guard module already loaded (the ``./py`` wrapper installs it before the script runs);
459	    else loads ``hn_guard/guards_v04.py`` by explicit path, never through sys.path. Loading it does not
460	    install anything.
461	    """
462	    for key in _GUARD_KEYS:
463	        mod = sys.modules.get(key)
464	        if mod is not None and hasattr(mod, "control_normal"):
465	            return mod.control_normal
466	    if __package__:
467	        from .hn_guard.guards_v04 import control_normal
468	
469	        return control_normal
470	    import importlib.util
471	
472	    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
473	    path = here.parent / "hn_guard" / "guards_v04.py"
474	    if not path.is_file():
475	        path = here / "hn_guard" / "guards_v04.py"
476	    key = _GUARD_KEYS[-1]
477	    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(key, path)
478	    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
479	    sys.modules[key] = mod
480	    try:
481	        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
482	    except BaseException:
483	        del sys.modules[key]
484	        raise
485	    return mod.control_normal
486	
487	
488	def control_direction(seed: int, like: Any) -> torch.Tensor:
489	    """A seeded Gaussian tensor with ``like``'s shape and Frobenius norm: the only randomness allowed.
490	
491	    Built on the guard's ``control_normal(seed, shape)`` (SHAKE-256, bit-identical everywhere), so it
492	    runs under KERNEL_CLIENT and BUILD_EDIT alike.
493	    """
494	    like = _f32(like)
495	    v = _control_normal()(int(seed), tuple(like.shape)).to(torch.float32)
496	    return v * (torch.linalg.vector_norm(like) / torch.linalg.vector_norm(v))
497	
498

"""Inspect metadata, label rows, final norm, embedding scale; count Qwen tokens of sample blocks."""
import json
import torch
from wsp import (ARCH, NAMES, SHAPES, LABEL_IDS, CLASS_NAMES, tok, label_rows, load, load_original,
                 budget, load_quota, edited, edit_hash)
import renderer

print("edited:", edited(), "hash:", edit_hash()[:12])
print("budget:", budget())
print("quota:", load_quota())
print("label ids:", LABEL_IDS, CLASS_NAMES)
arch = {k: v for k, v in ARCH.items() if k != "layer_types"}
print("arch:", json.dumps(arch)[:1500])
print("n names:", len(NAMES))
shapes_by_layer0 = {n: SHAPES[n] for n in NAMES if ".layers.0." in n or ".layers.3." in n or "embed" in n or n.endswith("norm.weight") and "layers" not in n}
for n, s in shapes_by_layer0.items():
    print(n, s)

rows = label_rows(original=True)
print("label row norms:", torch.linalg.vector_norm(rows, dim=1))
G = rows @ rows.T
print("label row gram:\n", G)
fn = load("model.language_model.norm.weight")
print("final norm w: mean", fn.mean().item(), "std", fn.std().item(), "min", fn.min().item(), "max", fn.max().item())
print("(1+w) rms:", torch.sqrt(((1 + fn) ** 2).mean()).item())

# token counts of grammar-sheet style blocks
samples = [
    "09:14:03.250 read_file path=zork/zeta/widget.qx lines=12-40 -> ok in=1840 out=96",

    print(repr(w), tok.encode(w, add_special_tokens=False).ids)

"""Analyse fwd call 1 (req_a02): per-window logits vs my labels, confusion, and class geometry at L24."""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from wsp import tok, label_lens, label_rows, load

CALL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "1"
META = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "output/wsp-a/scratch/meta_a02.json"
resp = json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{CALL}/response.json"))
meta = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(META))}
kind = "original" if resp["model"] == "original" else "edited"
CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
conf = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
rows = []
H = {}
for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
    m = meta[s["id"]]
    r = s[kind]
    print(f"== {s['id']}")
    for wi, w in enumerate(s["windows"]):
        lab = m["labels"][w]
        lg = r["label_logits"][wi]
        pred = int(np.argmax(lg))
        top = r["argmax"][wi]
        flag = ""
        if lab != "AMBIG":
            conf[CL.index(lab), pred] += 1
            flag = "ok" if CL.index(lab) == pred else "XX"
        print(f"  w{w:2d} {lab[:4]} pred={CL[pred][:4]} {flag:2s} logits={np.round(lg, 2)} top={repr(tok.decode([top]))}")
        rows.append((s["id"], w, lab, pred, lg))
print("confusion (rows=my label, cols=pred):")
print(conf)
print("acc:", np.trace(conf) / conf.sum())

# geometry at L24 (and other layers) over confident windows
for L in [24, 20, 16, 12]:
    X, Y = [], []
    for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
        m = meta[s["id"]]
        key = f"{kind}.s{si}.hidden.L{L}"
        a = np.load(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{CALL}/{resp['arrays'][key]['file']}")
        for wi, w in enumerate(s["windows"]):
            lab = m["labels"][w]
            if lab == "AMBIG":
                continue
            X.append(a[wi]); Y.append(CL.index(lab))
    X = torch.tensor(np.stack(X)); Y = torch.tensor(Y)
    print(f"--- layer {L}: n={len(Y)} per class={[(Y == c).sum().item() for c in range(4)]}, resid norm mean={X.norm(dim=1).mean():.1f}")
    # normalise like the final norm would (unit RMS) so that scale differences do not dominate
    Xn = X / X.pow(2).mean(1, keepdim=True).sqrt()
    mu = torch.stack([Xn[Y == c].mean(0) for c in range(4)])
    g = Xn.mean(0)
    D = mu - g
    # cosine between class directions
    Dn = D / D.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    print(" class-direction norms:", np.round(D.norm(dim=1).numpy(), 3))
    print(" cos between class directions:\n", np.round((Dn @ Dn.T).numpy(), 2))
    # nearest-class-mean accuracy with those directions (resubstitution; a sanity check of separability only)
    sc = Xn @ D.T
    pred = sc.argmax(1)
    cm = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
    for y, p in zip(Y.tolist(), pred.tolist()):
        cm[y, p] += 1
    print(" nearest-direction confusion:\n", cm)
    if L == 24:
        # how do the original label rows align with the class directions (in normed space incl. (1+w))
        w = load("model.language_model.norm.weight")
        E = label_rows(original=True)
        Eg = E * (1 + w)  # effective readout direction on unit-RMS residual
        print(" cos(label row (1+w), class dir):\n", np.round(((Eg / Eg.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)) @ Dn.T).numpy(), 3))
        # per-class projection stats of windows on each class direction
        for c in range(4):
            v = sc[:, c]
            print(f" dir {CL[c][:4]}: mean proj by true class", [round(v[Y == k].mean().item(), 2) for k in range(4)],
                  "std", [round(v[Y == k].std().item(), 2) if (Y == k).sum() > 1 else 0 for k in range(4)])

"""Analyse fwd call 1 (req_a02): per-window logits vs my labels, confusion, and class geometry at L24."""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from wsp import tok, label_lens, label_rows, load

CALL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "1"
META = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "output/wsp-a/scratch/meta_a02.json"
resp = json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{CALL}/response.json"))
meta = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(META))}
kind = "original" if resp["model"] == "original" else "edited"
CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
conf = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
rows = []
H = {}
for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
    m = meta[s["id"]]
    r = s[kind]
    print(f"== {s['id']}")
    for wi, w in enumerate(s["windows"]):
        lab = m["labels"][w]
        lg = r["label_logits"][wi]
        pred = int(np.argmax(lg))
        top = r["argmax"][wi]
        flag = ""
        if lab != "AMBIG":
            conf[CL.index(lab), pred] += 1
            flag = "ok" if CL.index(lab) == pred else "XX"
        print(f"  w{w:2d} {lab[:4]} pred={CL[pred][:4]} {flag:2s} logits={np.round(lg, 2)} top={repr(tok.decode([top]))}")
        rows.append((s["id"], w, lab, pred, lg))
print("confusion (rows=my label, cols=pred):")
print(conf)
print("acc:", np.trace(conf) / conf.sum())

# geometry at L24 (and other layers) over confident windows
for L in [24, 20, 16, 12]:
    X, Y = [], []
    for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
        m = meta[s["id"]]
        key = f"{kind}.s{si}.hidden.L{L}"
        a = np.load(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{CALL}/{resp['arrays'][key]['file']}")
        for wi, w in enumerate(s["windows"]):
            lab = m["labels"][w]
            if lab == "AMBIG":
                continue
            X.append(a[wi]); Y.append(CL.index(lab))
    X = torch.tensor(np.stack(X)); Y = torch.tensor(Y)
    print(f"--- layer {L}: n={len(Y)} per class={[(Y == c).sum().item() for c in range(4)]}, resid norm mean={X.norm(dim=1).mean():.1f}")
    # normalise like the final norm would (unit RMS) so that scale differences do not dominate
    Xn = X / X.pow(2).mean(1, keepdim=True).sqrt()
    mu = torch.stack([Xn[Y == c].mean(0) for c in range(4)])
    g = Xn.mean(0)
    D = mu - g
    # cosine between class directions
    Dn = D / D.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    print(" class-direction norms:", np.round(D.norm(dim=1).numpy(), 3))
    print(" cos between class directions:\n", np.round((Dn @ Dn.T).numpy(), 2))
    # nearest-class-mean accuracy with those directions (resubstitution; a sanity check of separability only)
    sc = Xn @ D.T
    pred = sc.argmax(1)
    cm = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
    for y, p in zip(Y.tolist(), pred.tolist()):
        cm[y, p] += 1
    print(" nearest-direction confusion:\n", cm)
    if L == 24:
        # how do the original label rows align with the class directions (in normed space incl. (1+w))
        w = load("model.language_model.norm.weight")
        E = label_rows(original=True)
        Eg = E * (1 + w)  # effective readout direction on unit-RMS residual
        print(" cos(label row (1+w), class dir):\n", np.round(((Eg / Eg.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)) @ Dn.T).numpy(), 3))
        # per-class projection stats of windows on each class direction
        for c in range(4):
            v = sc[:, c]
            print(f" dir {CL[c][:4]}: mean proj by true class", [round(v[Y == k].mean().item(), 2) for k in range(4)],
                  "std", [round(v[Y == k].std().item(), 2) if (Y == k).sum() > 1 else 0 for k in range(4)])

"""Write requests B01..B03: scenario set B split in three, every window, original model, activations."""
import json
from mk1 import write_request
from wsp import tok
import scen_b

sessions = scen_b.all_sessions()
ret = {"hidden": [12, 16, 20, 22, 23, 24], "mlp_act": [20, 21, 22, 23], "topk": 5}
parts = [sessions[0::3], sessions[1::3], sessions[2::3]]
counts = {}
for i, part in enumerate(parts, 1):
    req, meta = write_request(f"output/wsp-a/scratch/req_b0{i}.json", part, model="original", windows_mode="all",
                              ret=ret, meta_path=f"output/wsp-a/scratch/meta_b0{i}.json")
    total = 0
    for s in req["sessions"]:
        total += 167 + sum(len(tok.encode(b + "\n", add_special_tokens=False).ids) for b in s["blocks"]) + 11 * len(s["windows"])
    print(f"req_b0{i}: sessions={len(req['sessions'])} est tokens={total}")
    for m in meta:
        for l in m["labels"]:
            counts[l] = counts.get(l, 0) + 1
print("window label counts:", counts)
for s in sessions[:90:30]:
    labels, _ = s.labels()
    print("----", s.sid, " ".join(l[:4] for l in labels))
    print("\n".join(s.blocks()))

"""Pool fwd calls over a scenario set; baseline confusion; separability per layer; discriminative MLP neurons.
usage: ./py ana_b.py OUT.npz CALL:META [CALL:META ...]"""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from wsp import load, label_rows

out_path = sys.argv[1]
pairs = [a.split(":") for a in sys.argv[2:]]
CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
H_LAYERS, M_LAYERS = [12, 16, 20, 22, 23, 24], [20, 21, 22, 23]
data = {f"h{L}": [] for L in H_LAYERS}
data.update({f"m{L}": [] for L in M_LAYERS})
Y, LOG, SID, WIN, NBLK = [], [], [], [], []
conf = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
for call, metaf in pairs:
    resp = json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/response.json"))
    meta = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(metaf))}
    kind = "original" if resp["model"] == "original" else "edited"
    for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
        m = meta[s["id"]]
        r = s[kind]
        arrs = {}

"""Split-half check of direction quality: derive on sessions ending in _a, evaluate on _b (and vice versa).
Also time courses of a few top neurons. usage: ./py ana_b2.py setB_orig.npz"""
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch

d = np.load(sys.argv[1], allow_pickle=True)
Y, SID, WIN = d["Y"], d["SID"], d["WIN"]
CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
mask = Y >= 0
is_a = np.array([s.endswith("_a") for s in SID])


def dprime(a, b):
    return (a.mean() - b.mean()) / np.sqrt(0.5 * (a.var() + b.var()) + 1e-9)


def eval_dirs(key, normalise, k_sparse=None):
    X = torch.tensor(d[key]).double()
    if normalise:
        X = X / X.pow(2).mean(1, keepdim=True).sqrt()
    res = []
    for tr, te in ((is_a, ~is_a), (~is_a, is_a)):
        trm, tem = mask & tr, mask & te
        Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte = X[trm], Y[trm], X[tem], Y[tem]
        mu = torch.stack([Xtr[ytr == c].mean(0) for c in range(4)])
        g = Xtr.mean(0)
        D = mu - g
        if k_sparse:
            sd = torch.sqrt(torch.stack([Xtr[ytr == c].var(0) for c in range(4)]).mean(0) + 1e-6)
            for c in range(4):
                dn = (mu[c] - Xtr[ytr != c].mean(0)) / sd
                idx = dn.abs().topk(k_sparse).indices
                sp = torch.zeros_like(D[c]); sp[idx] = (mu[c] - Xtr[ytr != c].mean(0))[idx]
                D[c] = sp
        # one-vs-rest d' on test
        row = []
        for c in range(4):
            v = D[c] / D[c].norm()
            row.append(dprime((Xte[yte == c] @ v).numpy(), (Xte[yte != c] @ v).numpy()))
        # nearest-direction classifier with per-class threshold = midpoint of train class means along own dir
        S = Xte @ (D / D.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)).T
        Str = Xtr @ (D / D.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)).T
        # centre each score by the train mean over all classes (so biases are comparable)
        S = S - Str.mean(0)
        pred = S.argmax(1).numpy()
        cm = np.zeros((4, 4), int)
        for y, p in zip(yte, pred):
            cm[y, p] += 1
        res.append((row, cm))
    return res


for key, norm in [("h24", True), ("h23", True), ("h22", True), ("h20", True), ("h16", True), ("h12", True)]:
    r = eval_dirs(key, norm)
    print(f"--- {key} dense diff-of-means, split-half one-vs-rest d' (a->b, b->a):",
          [round(x, 2) for x in r[0][0]], [round(x, 2) for x in r[1][0]])
    cm = r[0][1] + r[1][1]
    print("    nearest-centred-direction confusion (both folds):\n", cm, " acc:", round(np.trace(cm) / cm.sum(), 3))
for key in ["m20", "m21", "m22", "m23"]:
    for k in (32, 128, None):
        r = eval_dirs(key, False, k)
        cm = r[0][1] + r[1][1]
        print(f"--- {key} sparse={k}: split-half one-vs-rest d'", [round(x, 2) for x in r[0][0]], [round(x, 2) for x in r[1][0]],
              " acc:", round(np.trace(cm) / cm.sum(), 3))
    print("    confusion (k=None):\n", cm)

# time courses of top neurons (from the full-data ranking in ana_b) in a few sessions
A = d["m23"]
for sid in ["S1_a", "S6_a", "R1_a", "P7_a", "O1_a", "O2_a", "P1_a"]:
    sel = np.where(SID == sid)[0]
    labs = [CL[Y[i]][:2] if Y[i] >= 0 else "--" for i in sel]
    print(sid, "labels:", " ".join(labs))
    for n in (2405, 2993, 1318, 1010, 2195, 3440, 857):
        print(f"   n{n}: " + " ".join(f"{A[i, n]:5.2f}" for i in sel))

"""Scenario set C: matched pairs. Each pair is two sessions with the same prefix that differ in one property:
REP (recent blocks repeat), REV (hunk ids return to earlier states), RES (latest status is a success after
errors), ERR (errors present), PROG (pass counts improving). Positive member first."""
from mk2 import Session, Ctx, explore, hnum, ftext, variant, PROJECTS

PAIRS = []  # (pair id, feature, sign, Session)


def mk(sid, pre, proj):
    s = Session(sid, start=["2026-03-01T09:14:03.250+00:00", "2026-03-02T14:02:11.000+00:00", "2026-03-04T03:21:45.100+00:00"][proj % 3])
    c = Ctx(s)
    c.P = PROJECTS[proj % len(PROJECTS)]
    if pre:
        explore(c, pre)
    return s, c


def pair(pid, feat, pos, neg):
    PAIRS.append((pid, feat, +1, pos))
    PAIRS.append((pid, feat, -1, neg))


# ---------------- REP: repeats vs distinct -------------------------------------------------------------
def rep_reads(pid, pre, proj, k):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    p = c.path()
    s.read(p)
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        s.read(p, eff="REDUNDANT")
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    for i in range(k):
        d.s.read(d.path(), lines=(5 * i + 1, 5 * i + 60) if i % 2 else None)
    pair(pid, "REP", s, t)


def rep_tests(pid, pre, proj, k):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    p = c.path()
    n = 9 + hnum(pid, hi=8)
    s.tests(c.suite(), n - 2, n, "NONE", error_class=c.err(), error_location=p)
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        s.tests(c.suite(), n - 2, n, "REDUNDANT", error_class=c.err(), error_location=p)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    for i in range(k):
        suite = d.P["suites"][i % 2]
        m = 6 + (i * 5) % 11
        if i % 3 == 1:
            d.s.tests(suite, m, m, "PROGRESS", dp=0.1)
        else:
            d.s.tests(suite, m - 1 - (i % 2), m, "NONE", error_class=d.err(i), error_location=d.path(i))
    pair(pid, "REP", s, t)


def rep_builds(pid, pre, proj, k, family="build"):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    p = c.path()
    s.build(c.target(), False, "NONE", error_class=c.err(2), error_location=p, family=family)
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        s.build(c.target(), False, "REDUNDANT", error_class=c.err(2), error_location=p, family=family)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    for i in range(k):
        tg = d.target() + ("" if i % 2 == 0 else "_" + d.P["suites"][1])
        d.s.build(tg, i % 3 == 1, "PROGRESS" if i % 3 == 1 else "NONE", dp=0.05 if i % 3 == 1 else 0,
                  error_class=None if i % 3 == 1 else d.err(i), error_location=d.path(i), family=family)
    pair(pid, "REP", s, t)


def rep_http(pid, pre, proj, k):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    loc = c.path(0)
    for i in range(k):
        s.http("PUT", c.P["host"], "/buckets/{b}/objects/{k}", False, "FAIL0" if i == 0 else "RETRY", error_class=c.err(1), error_location=loc)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    paths = ["/v1/images/{name}/push", "/jobs", "/v2/users/{id}", "/pipelines", "/v1/status/{id}", "/buckets/{b}", "/health", "/v3/items"]
    for i in range(k):
        ok = i % 3 != 1
        d.s.http(["GET", "POST", "PUT"][i % 3], d.P["host"], paths[i % len(paths)], ok, "NEW_FACT" if ok else "NONE",
                 error_class=None if ok else d.err(i), error_location=None if ok else d.path(i))
    pair(pid, "REP", s, t)


def rep_polls(pid, pre, proj, k):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)

    s.read(p, lines=(80, 140))
    s.edit(p, variant(base, 3, "repair"), dp=0.0)
    s.tests(c.suite(), n, n, "RESOLVES")

    p2 = d.path()
    b2 = d.base_text(p2)
    d.s.tests(d.suite(), n - 1, n, "FAIL0", error_class=d.err(2), error_location=p2)
    d.s.read(p2, lines=(80, 140))
    d.s.edit(p2, variant(b2, 3, "repair"), dp=0.0)
    d.s.tests(d.suite(), n - 1, n, "RETRY", error_class=d.err(2), error_location=p2)
    for ss, cc in ((s, c), (t, d)):
        if tail:
            explore(cc, tail, j0=3)

def res_build(pid, pre, proj, family="build", tail=0):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    p = c.path()
    base = c.base_text(p)
    s.build(c.target(), False, "FAIL0", error_class=c.err(2), error_location=p, family=family)
    s.edit(p, variant(base, 3, "repair"), dp=0.0)
    s.build(c.target(), True, "RESOLVES", family=family)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    p2 = d.path()
    b2 = d.base_text(p2)
    d.s.build(d.target(), False, "FAIL0", error_class=d.err(2), error_location=p2, family=family)
    d.s.edit(p2, variant(b2, 3, "repair"), dp=0.0)
    d.s.build(d.target(), False, "RETRY", error_class=d.err(2), error_location=p2, family=family)
    for ss, cc in ((s, c), (t, d)):
        if tail:
            explore(cc, tail, j0=3)
    pair(pid, "RES", s, t)


# ---------------- ERR: error present vs ok ------------------------------------------------------------------
def err_pair(pid, pre, proj, kind):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    p, p2 = c.path(), d.path()
    n = 11 + hnum(pid, hi=7)
    if kind == "tests":
        s.tests(c.suite(), n - 2, n, "NONE", error_class=c.err(), error_location=p)
        d.s.tests(d.suite(), n, n, "PROGRESS", dp=0.1)
    elif kind == "build":
        s.build(c.target(), False, "NONE", error_class=c.err(2), error_location=p)
        d.s.build(d.target(), True, "PROGRESS", dp=0.05)
    elif kind == "http":
        s.http("GET", c.P["host"], "/v1/status/{id}", False, "NONE", error_class=c.err(1), error_location=p)
        d.s.http("GET", d.P["host"], "/v1/status/{id}", True, "NEW_FACT")
    elif kind == "poll":
        s.poll(c.P["res"], "pending", "NONE", backoff=2)
        d.s.poll(d.P["res"], "ready", "NEW_FACT", backoff=2)
    elif kind == "read":
        s.read("missing/" + p, eff="NONE", outcome="ERROR", error_class="FileNotFound")
        d.s.read(p2)
    pair(pid, "ERR", s, t)


# ---------------- PROG: improving counts vs flat counts (fresh edits in both) -------------------------------
def prog_pair(pid, pre, proj, steps=3):
    s, c = mk(pid + "p", pre, proj)
    t, d = mk(pid + "n", pre, proj)
    n = 9 + hnum(pid, hi=8)
    for ss, cc, improving in ((s, c, True), (t, d, False)):
        p = cc.path()
        txt = cc.base_text(p)
        f0 = 4
        ss.tests(cc.suite(), n - f0, n, "NONE", error_class=cc.err(), error_location=p)
        for i in range(steps):
            txt = variant(txt, i + 1, f"e{i}")
            ss.edit(p, txt, dp=0.1 if improving else 0.0, eff="PROGRESS" if improving else "NONE")
            f = (f0 - (i + 1) * (f0 // steps + 1)) if improving else f0
            f = max(0, f) if i < steps - 1 or not improving else 0
            if f == 0:
                ss.tests(cc.suite(), n, n, "PROGRESS", dp=0.2)
            else:
                ss.tests(cc.suite(), n - f, n, "PROGRESS" if improving else "NONE", dp=0.1 if improving else 0.0,
                         error_class=cc.err(), error_location=p)
    pair(pid, "PROG", s, t)


def build_all():
    PAIRS.clear()
    j = 0
    for pre in (0, 2, 4):
        for proj in range(8):
            if (proj + pre) % 3 == 0:
                rep_reads(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 6 if proj % 2 else 4); j += 1
                rep_tests(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 6 if proj % 2 else 4); j += 1
                rev_ab(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 4, between=None if proj % 2 else "tests"); j += 1
                res_http(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 2, tail=proj % 3); j += 1
                err_pair(f"c{j}", pre, proj, ["tests", "build", "http", "poll", "read"][proj % 5]); j += 1
            if (proj + pre) % 3 == 1:
                rep_builds(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 6 if proj % 2 else 4, family="lint" if proj % 4 == 1 else "build"); j += 1
                rep_http(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 8 if proj % 2 else 4); j += 1
                rev_revert(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 3, between=None if proj % 2 else "build_ok"); j += 1
                res_poll(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 3, tail=proj % 3); j += 1
                prog_pair(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 3); j += 1
                rep_search(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 5); j += 1
            if (proj + pre) % 3 == 2:
                rep_polls(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 8 if proj % 2 else 4); j += 1
                rep_noop_edits(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 3); j += 1
                rev_write2(f"c{j}", pre, proj, 2); j += 1
                rev_abc(f"c{j}", pre, proj); j += 1
                res_tests(f"c{j}", pre, proj, tail=proj % 3); j += 1
                res_build(f"c{j}", pre, proj, family="lint" if proj % 2 else "build", tail=proj % 2); j += 1
                err_pair(f"c{j}", pre, proj, ["tests", "build", "http", "poll", "read"][(proj + 2) % 5]); j += 1
    return list(PAIRS)

"""Matched-pair feature directions from set C (calls 5-8), their consistency, and class projections on set B.
usage: ./py ana_c.py OUT.npz SETB.npz CALL:META ..."""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch

out_path, setb_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
pairs = [a.split(":") for a in sys.argv[3:]]
CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
LAYERS = [16, 20, 22, 23, 24]
sess = {}  # sid -> dict(h{L}: [n_win, d], labels, pair, feat, sign, logits)
for call, metaf in pairs:
    resp = json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/response.json"))
    meta = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(metaf))}
    for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
        m = meta[s["id"]]
        e = {"labels": m["labels"], "pair": m["pair"], "feat": m["feat"], "sign": m["sign"],
             "logits": np.array(s["original"]["label_logits"])}
        for L in LAYERS:
            e[f"h{L}"] = np.load(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/{resp['arrays'][f'original.s{si}.hidden.L{L}']['file']}")
        sess[s["id"]] = e


def unit_rms(x):
    x = torch.tensor(x).double()
    return x / x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True).sqrt()


feats = sorted({e["feat"] for e in sess.values()})
dirs = {}
print("pairs per feature:", {f: sum(1 for e in sess.values() if e["feat"] == f) // 2 for f in feats})
for L in LAYERS:
    print(f"=== layer {L}")
    for f in feats:
        deltas, deltas_prev = [], []
        for pid in sorted({e["pair"] for e in sess.values() if e["feat"] == f}):
            p, n = sess[pid + "p"], sess[pid + "n"]
            xp, xn = unit_rms(p[f"h{L}"]), unit_rms(n[f"h{L}"])
            deltas.append(xp[-1] - xn[-1])
            if len(xp) > 1 and len(xn) > 1:
                deltas_prev.append(xp[-2] - xn[-2])
        D = torch.stack(deltas)
        d = D.mean(0)
        dn = d / d.norm()
        proj = D @ dn
        Dp = torch.stack(deltas_prev)
        projp = Dp @ dn
        # leave-one-out consistency: direction from all other pairs, projection of the held-out pair
        loo = []
        for i in range(len(D)):
            di = (D.sum(0) - D[i]) / (len(D) - 1)
            loo.append(float(D[i] @ (di / di.norm())))
        loo = np.array(loo)
        print(f"  {f:4s}: |mean delta|={d.norm():.3f}  proj mean/std={proj.mean():.3f}/{proj.std():.3f} sign-agree={(proj > 0).float().mean():.2f}"
              f"  LOO mean/std={loo.mean():.3f}/{loo.std():.3f} agree={(loo > 0).mean():.2f}  prev-window agree={(projp > 0).float().mean():.2f}")
        dirs[f"{f}_L{L}"] = dn.float().numpy()
    M = torch.tensor(np.stack([dirs[f"{f}_L{L}"] for f in feats]))
    print("  cos between feature directions:\n", np.round((M @ M.T).numpy(), 2))

np.savez(out_path, **dirs, feats=np.array(feats))

# class projections on set B (confident windows), per layer
b = np.load(setb_path, allow_pickle=True)
Y = b["Y"]
mask = Y >= 0
for L in LAYERS:
    X = unit_rms(b[f"h{L}"][mask])
    y = Y[mask]
    print(f"=== set B projections, layer {L} (mean +- std by class; d' one-vs-rest in brackets)")
    for f in feats:
        v = torch.tensor(dirs[f"{f}_L{L}"]).double()
        s = (X @ v).numpy()
        parts = []
        for c in range(4):
            a, r = s[y == c], s[y != c]
            dp = (a.mean() - r.mean()) / np.sqrt(0.5 * (a.var() + r.var()))
            parts.append(f"{CL[c][:4]} {a.mean():6.2f}+-{a.std():4.2f} [{dp:5.2f}]")
        print(f"  {f:4s}: " + " | ".join(parts))

"""Residual structure at the readout (massive dims, mean direction), cross-layer stability of feature directions,
and the OSCI-vs-STAL contrast (set B) vs an edit-type-repetition contrast (set C)."""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch
from wsp import load, label_rows

CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
fd = np.load("output/wsp-a/scratch/feat_dirs.npz", allow_pickle=True)
b = np.load("output/wsp-a/scratch/setB_orig.npz", allow_pickle=True)
Y = b["Y"]; mask = Y >= 0


def unit_rms(x):
    x = torch.tensor(np.asarray(x)).double()
    return x / x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True).sqrt()


# 1. residual structure at L24 and L23
for L in (24, 23, 22, 20):
    X = unit_rms(b[f"h{L}"])
    m = X.mean(0)
    print(f"L{L}: |x|={X.norm(dim=1).mean():.2f} |mean|={m.norm():.2f} cos(x, mean) mean/min={((X @ m) / (X.norm(dim=1) * m.norm())).mean():.3f}/{((X @ m) / (X.norm(dim=1) * m.norm())).min():.3f}")
    top = m.abs().topk(8)
    print("   largest |mean| dims:", [(int(i), round(float(m[i]), 2)) for i in top.indices])
    sd = X.std(0)
    print("   their std across windows:", [round(float(sd[i]), 3) for i in top.indices], " median std:", round(float(sd.median()), 3))
    raw = torch.tensor(b[f"h{L}"]).double()
    print(f"   raw residual norm mean/std: {raw.norm(dim=1).mean():.2f}/{raw.norm(dim=1).std():.2f}; raw largest dims:",
          [(int(i), round(float(raw.mean(0)[i]), 2)) for i in raw.mean(0).abs().topk(5).indices])

# 2. cross-layer stability of feature directions
feats = list(fd["feats"])
for f in feats:
    vs = torch.tensor(np.stack([fd[f"{f}_L{L}"] for L in (16, 20, 22, 23, 24)]))
    print(f"{f}: cos across layers 16/20/22/23/24:\n", np.round((vs @ vs.T).numpy(), 2))

# 3. class contrasts on set B at L24 vs feature directions
X = unit_rms(b["h24"][mask]); y = Y[mask]
mu = torch.stack([X[y == c].mean(0) for c in range(4)])
g = X.mean(0)
F = torch.tensor(np.stack([fd[f"{f}_L24"] for f in feats])).double()
Fn = F / F.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
osc_stal = mu[3] - mu[2]
reco_stal = mu[1] - mu[2]
prod_rest = mu[0] - X[y != 0].mean(0)
print("|OSCI-STAL|=", round(float(osc_stal.norm()), 3), " cos with feats:", dict(zip(feats, np.round((Fn @ (osc_stal / osc_stal.norm())).numpy(), 2))))
print("|RECO-STAL|=", round(float(reco_stal.norm()), 3), " cos with feats:", dict(zip(feats, np.round((Fn @ (reco_stal / reco_stal.norm())).numpy(), 2))))
print("|PROD-rest|=", round(float(prod_rest.norm()), 3), " cos with feats:", dict(zip(feats, np.round((Fn @ (prod_rest / prod_rest.norm())).numpy(), 2))))

"""Edit-type repetition contrast from set C (rev positives whose last block is an edit/write or a revert, vs
rep positives whose last block is not an edit), compared with the OSCI-vs-STAL contrast of set B."""
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import torch

CL = ["PRODUCTIVE", "RECOVERY", "STALLED", "OSCILLATING"]
b = np.load("output/wsp-a/scratch/setB_orig.npz", allow_pickle=True)
Y = b["Y"]; mask = Y >= 0


def unit_rms(x):
    x = torch.tensor(np.asarray(x)).double()
    return x / x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True).sqrt()


X = unit_rms(b["h24"][mask]); y = Y[mask]
mu = torch.stack([X[y == c].mean(0) for c in range(4)])
g = X.mean(0)
osc_stal = mu[3] - mu[2]
sess = {}
for call, metaf in [a.split(":") for a in sys.argv[1:]]:
    resp = json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/response.json"))
    req = {s["id"]: s for s in json.load(open(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/request.json"))["sessions"]}
    meta = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(metaf))}
    for si, s in enumerate(resp["sessions"]):
        m = meta[s["id"]]
        sess[s["id"]] = {"feat": m["feat"], "sign": m["sign"], "blocks": req[s["id"]]["blocks"], "labels": m["labels"],
                         "h24": np.load(f"output/wsp-a/fwd/{call}/{resp['arrays'][f'original.s{si}.hidden.L24']['file']}")}
edit_rep, other_rep, revert_rep, fresh_edits = [], [], [], []
for sid, e in sess.items():
    last = e["blocks"][-1]
    x = unit_rms(e["h24"])[-1]
    if e["sign"] == 1:
        if e["feat"] == "REV" and last.split()[1] == "revert":
            revert_rep.append(x)
        elif e["feat"] == "REV" and last.split()[1] in ("edit_file", "write_file"):
            edit_rep.append(x)
        elif e["feat"] == "REP" and last.split()[1] not in ("edit_file",):
            other_rep.append(x)
    elif e["feat"] == "REV" and last.split()[1] in ("edit_file", "write_file"):
        fresh_edits.append(x)
edit_rep, other_rep, revert_rep, fresh_edits = [torch.stack(v) for v in (edit_rep, other_rep, revert_rep, fresh_edits)]
print("n edit-rep, other-rep, revert-rep, fresh-edits:", len(edit_rep), len(other_rep), len(revert_rep), len(fresh_edits))
d_er = edit_rep.mean(0) - other_rep.mean(0)
d_rv = revert_rep.mean(0) - other_rep.mean(0)
d_fe = fresh_edits.mean(0) - other_rep.mean(0)
cos = lambda a, c: round(float(a @ c / a.norm() / c.norm()), 3)
print("|edit-rep - other-rep|=", round(float(d_er.norm()), 3), " cos with OSCI-STAL:", cos(d_er, osc_stal))
print("|revert-rep - other-rep|=", round(float(d_rv.norm()), 3), " cos with OSCI-STAL:", cos(d_rv, osc_stal))
print("|fresh-edits - other-rep|=", round(float(d_fe.norm()), 3), " cos with OSCI-STAL:", cos(d_fe, osc_stal), " cos with edit-rep dir:", cos(d_fe, d_er))
print("cos(edit-rep dir, revert-rep dir):", cos(d_er, d_rv))
for name, v in (("edit-rep", d_er), ("revert-rep", d_rv), ("fresh-edits", d_fe), ("OSCI-STAL", osc_stal)):
    vn = v / v.norm()
    s = (X @ vn).numpy()
    a, r = s[y == 3], s[y == 2]
    print(f"  {name}: set B OSCI {a.mean():.2f}+-{a.std():.2f} vs STAL {r.mean():.2f}+-{r.std():.2f}  d'={(a.mean() - r.mean()) / np.sqrt(0.5 * (a.var() + r.var())):.2f}",
          " | RECO", round(float(s[y == 1].mean()), 2), "+-", round(float(s[y == 1].std()), 2), "PROD", round(float(s[y == 0].mean()), 2), "+-", round(float(s[y == 0].std()), 2))
np.savez("output/wsp-a/scratch/contrasts_L24.npz", osc_stal=osc_stal.float().numpy(), edit_rep=d_er.float().numpy(), revert_rep=d_rv.float().numpy(),
         fresh_edits=d_fe.float().numpy(), mean24=g.float().numpy(), mu=mu.float().numpy())
# what does the baseline model predict on the edit-rep vs other-rep sessions' last windows?
for name, keys in (("edit-rep", ("REV", 1, ("edit_file", "write_file"))), ("other-rep", ("REP", 1, None))):
    cnt = np.zeros(4, int)
    for sid, e in sess.items():
        if e["feat"] == keys[0] and e["sign"] == keys[1] and (keys[2] is None or e["blocks"][-1].split()[1] in keys[2]):
            pass
    print(name, "(see earlier fwd summaries for predictions)")
